_comment: Expansion 6 G.3: what the world keeps of a tale (game/story/consequences.py): the numbers of the ruin in full, the townsfolk's fates, newcomers, a holding's rent, a letter's weight, a song's reach; and the words of monuments, new names, relics, laws, holdings, letters and songs at inns. {hero} is the hero's first name; {villain}, {villain_short}, {beast}, {home} and {town} are the tale's.

monument_beast: Here {hero} killed {villain_short}, that took our sheep and our children. Let no one forget either.
To {hero}, who went into the dark at {home} and came back with {villain_short}'s head.
{villain_short} is dead. Raised by the people of {town} in thanks to {hero}.
For those {villain_short} took, and for {hero}, who ended it.
monument_gibbet: An iron cage hangs from the gibbet, and in it what is left of a captain of {gang}. A board beneath says: so end all who rob these roads.
The cage on the gibbet creaks in the wind. Somebody has chalked on the post: taken by {hero}, hanged by the lord.
A gibbet with a cage, and a captain of {gang} in it. The crows have been at him; the carters touch their caps as they pass.
monument_risen: Here {villain_short} sleeps at last. {hero} laid {him} down. Light a candle, and walk on.
A shrine to the dead of {home}, who walk no more. The people of {town} keep its candle lit.
For the {king} who walked, and for {hero}, who sent {him} back to the dark.
Rest. Cut beneath, in a rougher hand: and stay there.
relic_beast: tusk of {villain_short}, as long as a hand
relic_risen: rusted sword of the {king} who walked
ring of {villain_short}, cold to the touch
relic_risen_hero: black ring of {villain_short}, that no longer burns
cause_failed: put aside by their own people, who said they did nothing while {town} suffered
stepped down, broken by what happened to {town}
cause_risen: taken by the dead of {home}, on the night {town} fell
dragged into the dark by {villain_short}'s dead
ruin_news: {place} has fallen. The few who are left live in the shells of their houses, and bury their dead.
{place} is a ruin now. Those who could fled down the roads; the rest are in the ground.
There is no town at {place} any more: roofless walls, open doors, new graves and a handful who stayed.
{place} fell, and nobody came. What is left would not fill a village.
law_harshness: {realm} hardens its law: since the business with {gang}, justice in its lands is {value}.
In the lands of {realm} the gallows are busy now. Its justice is {value}, they say, and shamed into it.
{realm} has changed its law after {gang}: its judges are {value} now, and the roads are watched.
land_name: a holding near {place}, with three farms and a mill
the manor of Hollin Garth, near {place}
a farmstead and its fields outside {place}
lands on the river by {place}, with tenants who pay on quarter days
letter_line: To all who serve {realm}: the bearer, {hero}, has done this realm a service it will not forget. Help them as you would help me.
Whoever reads this, in {realm}'s name: open your doors to {hero}, who did for {place} what we could not.
Let {hero} pass, and be given what they need. I answer for them myself.
The bearer is a friend of {realm}. Treat them as one, or answer to me.
song_at_inn: After the meal {singer} sings {title}. The whole room knows the chorus; some of them glance at you.
Someone calls for {title}, and {singer} obliges. It is about you, more or less, and the room cheers the end.
{singer} sings {title} by the fire. They have made you taller in it, and braver; nobody asks you if it is true.
The room goes quiet for {title}. When {singer} is done, a man at the next table raises his cup to you.
vignette_ruined: {place} is a ruin now. A few chimneys stand, and a few people live among them, in the rooms that still have roofs.
Nettles grow in the square at {place}. The ones who stayed keep to the temple, and the crows keep to the rest.
At {place} the doors hang open and the wells are full of leaves. Somebody still lights a lamp in one window.
vignette_occupied: Strange banners hang over the gate at {place}, and strangers keep its watch. The people keep their heads down.
{place} pays its taxes to new masters now. The old lord's men are gone, and nobody says where.
At {place} the market still runs, but every cart is searched, and the new watch takes its cut.
vignette_cursed: The cows at {place} give sour milk, and the bread will not rise. People say the place is cursed, and leave when they can.
Nothing grows well at {place} now. The priests have blessed the fields twice, and the blight comes back.
At {place} the children dream the same dream, and will not say what it is.
vignette_emptied: Half the houses at {place} stand empty. The ones left behind count who did not come back.
{place} is quiet, too quiet: the people who fled have not come home, and the fields go to seed.
At {place} there are more graves than there were, and fewer people to tend them.
vignette_burned: The black beams of {place} still smell of smoke. They are clearing it, a cart at a time.
{place} burned. Where the houses were there is ash, and the people sleep in barns and in the church.
At {place} the fire took the roofs, and the winter will take more if the timber does not come.
vignette_rebuilding: At {place} there is scaffolding on every second house, and the sound of saws from dawn till dark.
{place} is building again. New thatch, new beams, and a few new faces among the old.
The wheelwrights and the masons are busy at {place}. It will never be what it was, people say, and they build anyway.
vignette_haunted: At {place} they bar the doors at dusk, and the dogs will not go near the old graves.
People at {place} still see lights on the hill at night, and nobody goes up to look.
{place} keeps its dead badly: there are footsteps in empty rooms, and the bell rings by itself.
vignette_memorial: In the square at {place} a memorial stands, and there are always flowers at its foot.
{place} has raised a stone for what happened. Children climb it; old people stop and read it.
At {place} the memorial is the first thing a traveller sees, and the people make sure of it.
vignette_festival: {place} is decked for a feast: garlands over the doors, and music in the square till late.
At {place} they have not stopped celebrating. There is a feast-day now, and your name is in its songs.
Lanterns hang across the streets of {place}, and the inns are full.
vignette_renamed: The place that was {old} is called {place} now, on the maps and in the mouths of carters.
Nobody calls it {old} any more. It is {place}, and they tell travellers why.
{place}, the people call it now. The old name, {old}, is only in the old songs.
vignette_laid: {place} is only a grave now. The grass has grown back over the stones, and the cold has gone out of the ground.
At {place} the dead keep still. A shepherd sleeps there in summer, and wakes rested.
The barrow at {place} is quiet. Somebody has left a cup of milk at the door, as the old people did.
vignette_cleared: {place} is empty now. The bones have been carried out, and the wind goes in and out of it as it likes.
Nothing lives at {place} but bats and foxes. The hunters walk past it without lowering their voices.
At {place} the old stink has gone, and the first brambles are growing over the way in.
vignette_held: {place} is still what it was. Nobody goes near it, and the paths round it are growing over.
At {place} nothing has changed, and that is the worst of it. The smoke still rises there at night.
{place} waits. The people who live in sight of it keep their shutters closed.
epilogue_realm_won: {ruler} of {realm} heard of it within the month. There were words said at court, and a cup raised to the one who ended it.
In {realm} they say {ruler} spoke of you at table: a name to remember, and to use, perhaps.
{realm} took it as its own victory, as realms do. {ruler} sent riders to {town} to make sure everyone knew whose land it was.
epilogue_realm_lost: {ruler} of {realm} did nothing, or nothing anyone saw. The tax-men still came to {town}, a little later than before.
In {realm} there was talk of soldiers and of hunts, and none came. {ruler} had other troubles.
{realm} counted what it lost and wrote it down. {ruler} sent condolences, and no help.
epilogue_realm_abandoned: {ruler} of {realm} has not heard your name. It is better that way, perhaps.
In {realm} the trouble at {town} is a line in a steward's letter, and nobody has read it yet.
{realm} goes on as it did. Whatever happens at {town} now, it will happen without you.
epilogue_sequel_heir: But the shepherds near {place} say they have seen tracks again: smaller, and fresh. {villain_short} did not die alone in the world.
There was a litter, it seems. Something of {villain_short}'s blood has gone to ground at {place}, and it is growing.
A woodcutter near {place} swears he heard it: the same cry, younger. The old ones say the get of a beast like that remembers.
epilogue_sequel_vacuum: The roads were quiet for a week. Then a new band took up where the old one left off: {gang}, out of {place}.
Where one gang falls another stands up. They call themselves {gang} now, and they have their hideout at {place}.
Not everyone who rode with the old band was taken. The rest found a new captain, and a new name: {gang}.
epilogue_sequel_returns: And yet the cold has not gone out of {place}. What you put down there is not done with the world, nor with you.
The priests at {town} do not ring the bell for it. They say the dead who keep their anchor come back, and they are waiting.
At {place} the ground is still cold. {villain_short} will walk again, and will remember whose hand it was.
sequel_told_heir: Word on the road: something has come down from {place} on the farms - young, they say, and as savage as {villain_short} ever was.
You hear it at a well: tracks by {place}, smaller than the old beast's, and sheep gone. {villain_short}'s blood is hunting.
A carter tells you: the get of {villain_short} is grown, and it has found its way out of {place}.
sequel_told_vacuum: Word on the road: {gang} is robbing the carts again out of {place}. The gap you left did not stay empty for long.
You hear it at an inn: a new band, {gang}, has the roads near {place} now. Some of the faces are the old ones.
A pedlar says the roads by {place} are bad again: {gang}, and a captain who wants the old one's name.
hero_standing: In {realm} your name stands at {standing} now.
{realm} holds you {standing} now, and says so.
hero_title: They call you {title} there, and mean it.
You are {title} now, by their word.
{title}: it is written down, with a seal.
hero_fame: Your name goes before you on the roads: more people know it than you will ever meet.
Strangers have heard of you now. Some of them want to see if it is true.
In the inns of three counties they know your name, and argue about what you did.
hero_infamy: Your name goes before you on the roads, and doors close when it does.
Mothers know your name now, and use it to frighten their children.
In the inns they lower their voices when you come in.
